title: A floating telescope?
caption: The Danish 1.54-meter telescope reflected in a roadside mirror, La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A domed telescope seems to float in mid-air, as if framed in a roadside picture. The effect is a trick of perspective and clever camerawork. The Danish 1.54-meter telescope is reflected, perfectly framed, in one of the many roadside mirrors around ESO's La Silla Observatory.

In the reflection, the telescope appears to point at the Large Magellanic Cloud, which shows in the upper left. The LMC is a small galaxy close by, in orbit around the Milky Way. A soft green airglow, faint light given off by Earth's atmosphere, sweeps across the sunset sky thanks to the very sensitive technique used. Faint orange halos in the distance mark faraway towns and cities beyond the mountains.
La Silla sits at 2400 meters on the edge of the Chilean Atacama Desert and has been an ESO stronghold since the 1960s. ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky took the picture.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph by Yuri Beletsky, taken with a very sensitive technique that picks up faint airglow. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: The camera records faint light, such as the green airglow and the glow of distant towns, far more strongly than the eye would see it.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: La Silla currently runs two four-meter-class telescopes that rank among the most productive in the world, according to ESO. The source describes this reflected view of the Danish telescope as a never-before-seen snapshot of the site.
alt: A telescope dome reflected in a roadside mirror so it seems to float, under a sunset sky with a faint green glow and the Large Magellanic Cloud at upper left.
